data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The safest reclamation protocol is a generation-tracked consensus lease protocol that requires proof-of-absence before reclaiming any workspace associated with a generation.","counterconditions":[{"case":"A consensus group partition during reclamation can void the safety guarantee by allowing a minority to issue a stale or forged proof-of-absence.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Corruption of the generation registry itself cascades into wrongful reclamation if the registry is not itself protected by the same consensus layer.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Asynchronous evidence commits from the crashed process may race with the proof-of-absence issuance, allowing completed evidence to be displaced before it is observed.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"A generation registry durably records the count and identity of completed evidence nodes per generation. When a process crashes without a terminal record, its workspace cannot be reclaimed until a consensus lease among surviving witnesses issues a proof-of-absence asserting that no evidence nodes from that workspace have been merged into the completed set.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
